name: Renewal and rent / fee escalation
why: Renewal that only one side controls, or open-ended increases, can force you to move or pay much more at short notice.
fair_standard: Renewal by mutual written consent, with the yearly increase fixed up front. In Indian rentals a 5% to 10% annual increase is typical, and the Model Tenancy Act 2021 expects rent revisions to follow the agreement or come with 3 months' written notice.

name: One-sided right to change terms
patterns: as (the owner|the company|the client) may decide
why: The other party can change price, scope or rules after you sign. A WhatsApp message or intranet post is not real consent.
fair_standard: Changes only by a written amendment signed by both parties. Under the Indian Contract Act 1872 a contract needs mutual consent, so 'continued stay or work means acceptance' clauses are weak.

name: One-sided arbitration
why: If the other side alone picks the arbitrator, sets a far-away seat or makes you pay the fees, the dispute process is stacked against you.
fair_standard: Arbitrator chosen jointly, or by an arbitral institution or court, with costs shared and the seat where you live or work. Indian courts have held that a party interested in the dispute cannot unilaterally appoint a sole arbitrator (Perkins Eastman v. HSCC, Supreme Court 2019, reaffirmed by a Constitution Bench in 2024). For small rental disputes, the Rent Authority or Civil Court is usually cheaper.

name: Liability cap or waiver
why: If the other party causes you harm or doesn't pay, what you can recover may be capped at a token amount.
fair_standard: A mutual cap of at least the full contract value, with no cap on unpaid fees or on fraud, gross negligence, wilful misconduct or data breaches.

name: One-way indemnity
why: You may have to pay the other party's losses and legal costs, even for problems they caused, such as building defects or content they supplied.
fair_standard: Mutual indemnities, each limited to that party's own breach or negligence and capped. Never an indemnity for the other party's own defects or instructions.

name: Lock-in, forfeiture and one-sided termination
why: Leaving early could cost you your whole deposit or a large penalty, while the other side can exit freely.
fair_standard: A lock-in that binds both sides equally, and leaving early costs at most the rent or fee for the remaining lock-in or notice period. Under Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act 1872, courts award only reasonable compensation, not a fixed penalty out of proportion to the actual loss.

name: Late fees, penalties and hidden charges
why: Daily penalties and inflated utility rates quickly exceed what you actually owe.
fair_standard: A grace period (rent is commonly due by the 5th to 10th), a modest fixed late fee or interest, and electricity billed at the actual DISCOM tariff (e.g. BESCOM, MSEDCL) shown on the bill, without a markup.

name: Security deposit terms
why: Very large deposits and vague or automatic deductions make it easy to keep your money.
fair_standard: The Model Tenancy Act 2021 caps residential deposits at 2 months' rent (6 months for commercial), refundable when you hand over the premises. Deductions only for actual damage beyond normal wear and tear, with receipts. The Act is a model law adopted by only some states, and Bengaluru often asks for more, but it is a strong negotiating benchmark.

name: Cutting utilities or locking you out
why: Self-help eviction or cutting water or electricity to force payment is coercive and unlawful in most states.
fair_standard: The Model Tenancy Act 2021 and state rent control laws prohibit a landlord from withholding essential supplies such as water and electricity. Arrears must be recovered through the Rent Authority or the courts.

name: Entry, inspection and monitoring
patterns: at any time, with or without notice
why: Broad access or monitoring rights erode your privacy.
fair_standard: The Model Tenancy Act 2021 requires at least 24 hours' written notice, with visits between 7 am and 8 pm. In employment, monitoring should be limited to company systems and disclosed in writing, not your personal devices or accounts.

name: Repair and maintenance burden
why: Making the tenant pay for structural, seepage or wiring work means paying to maintain the owner's property.
fair_standard: Under the Model Tenancy Act 2021 the landlord handles structural repairs, whitewashing, plumbing and wiring replacement, and the tenant handles minor day-to-day repairs (switches, taps) and damage they cause.

name: Stamp duty and registration
why: Paying every cost alone is unusual, and an unregistered or under-stamped agreement is harder to rely on as evidence.
fair_standard: Stamp duty and registration costs are commonly shared equally. Leases of 12 months or more must be registered under the Registration Act 1908, and the Model Tenancy Act expects tenancies to be reported to the Rent Authority. Ensure correct state stamp duty is paid.

name: Lifestyle and personal restrictions
why: Blanket rules on food, guests or who you live with limit your normal use of your home.
fair_standard: House rules should be reasonable, written and agreed before you sign. Blanket bans on food, visitors or family members are negotiable and may be unenforceable or discriminatory.

name: Service bond and retained documents
why: A large fixed bond or holding your original certificates can trap you in a job.
fair_standard: Indian courts generally enforce bonds only to recover actual, proven training costs as reasonable compensation (s.74 Indian Contract Act), reduced pro rata for time served. Employers should not keep your original certificates; offer attested copies instead.

name: Unequal or very long notice period
why: Long notice for you but short notice for them restricts your job moves while leaving you unprotected.
fair_standard: Equal notice on both sides. 30 to 60 days is common outside senior roles, with an option to buy out notice and to adjust earned leave against it.

name: Pay, deductions and unpaid work
why: Open-ended deductions, discretionary pay or unpaid extra work cut into what you actually earn.
fair_standard: Only deductions permitted by law or specifically agreed in writing (Code on Wages 2019), variable pay with written criteria, overtime or comp-off for extra days as required by the Shops and Establishments Act, and paid change requests beyond a fixed number of revisions.

name: Slow or conditional payment (freelance)
why: Long payment cycles, no advance and approval-based payment let the client delay or avoid paying.
fair_standard: An advance of 30% to 50%, milestone payments within 30 to 45 days of invoice (the MSMED Act 2006 requires payment to registered micro and small enterprises within 45 days, so get Udyam registration), GST charged on top of the fee, and TDS deducted only as per law with Form 16A issued.

name: Broad IP ownership grab
why: You may hand over your past work, personal projects or reusable tools, sometimes before you are even paid.
fair_standard: Assign only work created for the job or project, passing on full payment. Exclude prior inventions, personal projects on your own time and equipment, and your pre-existing tools (license those instead). Keep the right to show the work in your portfolio.

name: Post-exit non-compete / exclusivity
why: This can stop you working in your field for years after the job or project ends.
fair_standard: Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act 1872 makes post-termination restraints on trade generally void, and courts routinely refuse to enforce them. Restrictions during the engagement, confidentiality, and reasonable non-solicitation of clients and staff are usually upheld.

name: Personal data use and sharing
why: Your Aadhaar, PAN and personal accounts could be shared or monitored far beyond what the job needs.
fair_standard: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023, personal data may be processed only for a specified purpose with consent. You can withdraw consent and ask for erasure, and Aadhaar should be collected only where legally required.

name: Unlimited transfer / relocation
why: A clause allowing transfer anywhere can be used to force a resignation.
fair_standard: Transfers limited to named cities, with your consent for overseas postings, and relocation costs paid by the employer.

name: Distant seat or jurisdiction
why: Disputes heard in another city make it costly and impractical to enforce your rights.
fair_standard: Courts or seat in the city where you live or where the property or work is located.
